title: A Podcast on Nusaybah's Courage at Uhud
script: Host: [thoughtful] Welcome back to the show. Today my guest is Ridwan, who studies the roles women played in the earliest battles of Islam. Thanks for joining me.
Guest: Thank you for having me. Nusaybah bint Ka'ab is a figure I could discuss for hours without running out of material.
Host: [carefully] I've heard she is remembered mainly for the Battle of Uhud. What exactly did she do there?
Guest: She originally went to the battlefield to give water to the wounded, not expecting to fight at all that day.
Guest: [reflective] However, when the battle suddenly turned chaotic and enemy soldiers surrounded the Prophet, she picked up a sword without hesitation.
Host: So she went from carrying water to defending the Prophet directly? That's a remarkable shift in just a few moments.
Guest: [honestly] Exactly, and despite receiving several serious wounds herself, she kept fighting, positioning her own body between the Prophet and the attackers.
Host: Did the Prophet ever acknowledge what she had done that day?
Guest: [seriously] He did, and later he reportedly said that wherever he looked during the worst moments, he saw Nusaybah defending him.
Host: That's an extraordinary compliment, especially considering how many soldiers were fighting around him at the same time.
Guest: [gently] It is, and if she hadn't acted so quickly, some historians argue the outcome of that chaotic moment could have been far worse.
Host: Did her courage end after that particular battle, or did she continue serving afterward?
Guest: [encouraging] She continued for years, even losing a hand in a later battle, yet she never stopped supporting the community she believed in.
Host: It sounds like her story challenges the idea that only men shaped those early, dangerous years of Islam.
Guest: [sincere] Precisely. Even though history often focuses on male commanders, Nusaybah's bravery proves that assumption was never entirely accurate.
Host: Thank you, Ridwan, for reminding us of a courage that deserves far more recognition than it usually receives.
Guest: [thoughtful] Thank you for having me. I hope her story inspires listeners to look closer at the women behind these events.
